verdict.rationale: The IRS documents two sanctioned third-party rails through which a provider can act for a company. For EIN applications, a third-party designee may apply with signed authorization from the responsible party. For e-filing, providers can enroll as Authorized IRS e-file Providers, with a published approval timeline and suitability steps such as fingerprinting. Missing for 10: any documented general representative or power-of-attorney rail for account-level actions beyond EIN applications and e-filing, and independent or hands-on corroboration of how the designee flow works in practice.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, the service documents a sanctioned third-party rail — designees, authorized providers, registered agents, or representatives — through which a provider can act for my company

citations.quote: a third-party designee may apply, with signed authorization from the responsible party
